cards.card: VISA Gold Digital / Mastercard Gold Digital
VISA Platinum Digital / Mastercard World Digital

note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): Ameriabank, Ardshinbank and ACBA Bank; only Ameriabank's documents, already found, were read again this time, for want of the research's budget. Ameriabank's lending terms for unsecured credit cards (edition 69, effective 7 July 2026), read in full on 2026-10-30: 21% a year in drams on a VISA Classic or Mastercard Standard card (15% to 21% when scored, written at its top, as read on 2026-10-29), 20% on the Gold, World (formerly Platinum), Platinum and Signature cards and their digital versions, and 19% on the VISA Infinite and Mastercard World Elite; a grace period of up to 51 days; a minimum payment of 10% of the amount used or 5,000 drams, whichever is greater, plus accrued interest; a lump-sum fee of 5,000 drams for a minimum not paid when due (written as the late fee); and a fine of 0.13% a day on the overdue loan and interest, written as a penalty rate of 47.45% a year (0.13% times 365). The rate rises by 0.25% to 0.5% in cases the game doesn't model. Its card rates and fees (edition 46, effective 7 July 2026), the credit card with a grace period: a card issued by scoring is a VISA Classic or Mastercard Standard with no annual service fee (the card already written); the others are issued free and charge an annual service fee (Gold 20,000 drams, Gold digital 7,500, Platinum or World 30,000, its digital 15,000, Signature 60,000, Signature digital 40,000, Infinite or World Elite 100,000; the lower fees when ordered through the MyAmeria app, and the monthly alternatives, aren't written). A cash withdrawal at Ameriabank's ATMs costs 2% (2.2% at its counters and 2.5%, at least 2,500 drams, elsewhere; not written). The Classic Digital card isn't written: a card issued by scoring is the Classic or Standard. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): no bank was added. Tried: ACBA Bank's tariffs page links twelve tariff documents; none of them, nor its payment card tariff (in Armenian), was read for a credit card rate in the time; Inecobank answered with a Cloudflare check; Ardshinbank, Evocabank and IDBank's home pages linked no credit card terms.
